Q: Simple Mui TextField crashing in RTL locale A:

enter image description hereRoot Cause: Why Did the Crash Happen?

The crash occurs due to a known parsing bug in stylis-plugin-rtl (tracked under Issue #46 on the plugin repository) and how it interacts with the Stylis preprocessor (which compiles CSS for Emotion / Material-UI).

Here is the step-by-step reason for the behavior:

  1. RTL-Only Activation: Your localization setup loads stylis-plugin-rtl only when the active locale is Right-to-Left (e.g., Arabic, ar). When rendering in English (en), the RTL plugin is not loaded, which is why the code works perfectly fine there.

  2. Parsing Breakdown: When the Arabic locale is active, Stylis runs the CSS string through stylis-plugin-rtl. When the plugin encounters a nested descendant selector combined with a double-colon (::) pseudo-element—specifically "& .MuiInputBase-input::placeholder"—its internal tokenization/regex fails to parse the selector structure correctly.

  3. The Unhandled Exception: Because the parser gets confused by the space followed by the double-colon pseudo-element, it fails to initialize the target node structure. When the prefixer/utility tries to insert the prefixed versions (::-webkit-input-placeholder, ::-moz-placeholder, etc.) by calling .push() on the node's AST structure, it attempts to read .push on undefined, triggering the runtime error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push')

Alternate Solutions to Style the Placeholder Text

To fix the crash, you need to avoid targeting the ::placeholder pseudo-element through a nested child class in the root sx prop. Here are two clean, standard ways to do it:

Option 1: Pass the Style to inputProps (Recommended)

Instead of applying the style to the root element wrapper and targeting the input, you can pass the style directly to the underlying <input> element using inputProps. This allows you to use a simple selector (&::placeholder) which is parsed perfectly by stylis-plugin-rtl in both LTR and RTL.

jsx

<TextField

placeholder={'Enter your name'}

inputProps={{

sx: {

'&::placeholder': {

color: 'blue',

opacity: 1, // Set to 1 to override default browser opacity styling

  },

},

}}

/>

Option 2: Target the input tag in sx

If you prefer to keep the sx prop on the parent TextField element, you can simplify the selector chain by targeting the input tag directly instead of the full .MuiInputBase-input class:enter image description here

jsx

<TextField

placeholder={'Enter your name'}

sx={{

'& input::placeholder': {

color: 'blue',

opacity: 1,

},

}}

/>

Q: What is XOR RAX, RAX MOV RDI, [PTR] REP STOSQ A:

This is AMD64 machine code.

xor rax, rax   -- sets the value of rax to zero
mov rdi, [ptr] -- loads the value of ptr into the rdi register
rep stosq      -- repeats stores of the rax value to [rdi] 
                  rcx number of times, rdi is incremented after each store

Q: Why doesn't it use all available RAM? A:

It is bad manners for a program to lay claim to huge amounts of memory unless it actually needs to use it.

Q: I would appreciate some advice about types in Python A:

Is it actually a good practice to declare a type for every single variable and method?

In the Public API that you design, in its various signatures: "yes!".

For local variables: typically "no", as we expect their types can be automatically inferred.

Annotations of a signature serve as valuable documentation to humans, and can let linters like pyright point out bugs before you've written even a single test.

In code I author, I make mypy --strict and ruff check part of my routine edit--debug cycle. So signatures always mention the gozinta and gowzoutta type, even for a private def _helper().

ruff is very fast, and there are some optional checks you might choose to turn on. Consider this tiny bit of code:

def square(n):
    return n * n

By selecting some optional ANNotation checks in the [tool.ruff.lint] section of pyproject.toml, we can obtain helpful reminders like these:

ANN001 Missing type annotation for function argument `n`
ANN201 Missing return type annotation for public function `square`

Once your project under development lints clean, it's easy to keep it that way, even while adding many new features. Frequent linting checks ensure there's only one function that needs tidying up, and it's the one that is top-of-mind since it's the one mostly recently added or changed.

Occasionally you will want to annotate local variables.

def foo(a: float, b: float) -> None:
    total = a + b
    xs = list(range(6))
    ys = []
    # Now .append() several numbers to `ys`
    ...

The first two are easily inferred, so there's no need to write explicit types such as these:

    total: float = a + b
    xs: list[int] = list(range(6))

But an empty container poses a challenge for type inference. So you might need to explicitly write:

    ys: list[float] = []

Another possibility would be to prefer a list comprehension:

    ys = [n * n
          for n in range(6)]

which implicitly gives us a list[int] type.

Q: Execute external bash script inside GitLab-ci Docker build A:

The simple answer is, you don't: you are using the gitlab-runners docker executor and jobs do not have access to files on the host.

One of the following seems the simplest solution to getting access to the host.

  1. Create an additional gitlab-runner instance, using the "shell" executor. This will run scripts on the host. You can use tags to target this specific runner from a deployment job.

  2. Alternatively, use a docker executor based gitlab runner that mounts /var/run/docker.sock in its config.toml settings. this will give docker commands running in the script: access to the hosts docker instance so you can simply script the deployment from a deployment job.

Q: Querying only unwatched videos for a subscription using the Youtube API A:

I Haven't tried this yet, but using the YouTube Analytics API instead of the YouTube Data API, you might be able to get what you want: request a report where metrics=views and dimension=video, and sort by views in ascending order.

For example:

https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/analytics/v1/reports
  ?metrics=views
  &dimensions=video
  &sort=views
  &ids={your channel id}

One thing that I would be concerned about with this approach is that if YOU watch a video yourself, as a part of the upload/sanity check process, the views count will be non-zero. Also note that there is a sizable delay between when a video is viewed, and when that view is reported via the analytics api - it could be anywhere from 24 to 36 hrs.

Q: Scraping and downloading M4S Segmented Audio & Video Files A:

usually such segmented video files have a playlist.m3u8 or manifest.mpd file

in your case it is a manifest.mpd file at https://5a153f939af4b.streamlock.net/academy/77794/manifest.mpd?tID=432689&videoView=1&accessToken=xxx

but direct access returns HTTP 403 Forbidden, so you need a valid accessToken to download the manifest.mpd file

now you can pass the manifest.mpd file to yt-dlp like

yt-dlp --enable-file-urls file://"$PWD"/manifest.mpd

but this fails in this case, because yt-dlp fails to parse the Location element <Location>https://5a153f939af4b.streamlock.net/academy/77794/manifest_xxx.mpd</Location>

workaround: patch the file URLs in manifest.mpd

sed -i.bak -E 's,(media|initialization)=",\1="https://5a153f939af4b.streamlock.net/academy/77794/,g' manifest.mpd

now yt-dlp should download manifest.mp4

Q: How to save a Unicode character to a text file A:

On Windows Microsoft Access VBA I use this simple Byte Array method to save a string in a utf-8 file:

' This function saves a string into a utf8 file.
' inputs:
'   strIn: in string
'   strFilename: destination Filename
' locals:
'   iunit: file unit number
'   ByteArray: Byte Array
'
Function SaveAsUtf8(ByVal strIn As String, ByVal strFilename As String)
  Dim iunit As Integer
  Dim ByteArray() As Byte
 
' get file unit:
  iunit = FreeFile()
 
' Open strFilename For Binary Access Write As iunit
  Open strFilename For Binary As iunit

' ByteArray is required:
  ByteArray = strIn

  Put #iunit, , ByteArray

  Close iunit

  SaveAsUtf8 = 1
End Function

Sub test()
  Dim strIn As String
 
  strIn = "This file has some Chinese ideograms " & ChrW(&H9171) & ChrW(&H6CB9) & " - Soy Sauce."
  SaveAsUtf8 strIn, "C:\temp\myutf8.txt"
End Sub

When I open myutf8.txt file, I have this string in it:

This file has some Chinese ideograms 酱油 - Soy Sauce.
